newsitem.title: USA: International Multifoods sees vending turnaround.
newsitem.headline: International Multifoods sees vending turnaround.

text.p: International Multifoods Inc said it is on track to turn around its vending business, which has suffered from soft margins.

"Despite seasonal pressures on our vending distribution business in the first half of the fiscal year, we are increasingly confident that we are on track to turn this unit around," Gary Costley, chairman, said in a statement.
Multifoods on Thursday reported earnings of $0.11 a share for the fiscal first quarter ended May 31 compared with year-ago results of $0.10 before a $0.12 charge.

Foodservice Distribution, which includes the vending distribution business, had operating earnings of $4.1 million in the first quarter, down from $5.1 million a year ago. Sales were $449.4 million, up from $443.3 million a year ago.

The company said Foodservice earnings were hurt by a slowdown in the food exporting business with a major customer in Russia and slightly lower margins in vending distribution. The vending distribution business was affected by continued margin softness associated with price competition, it added.
North America Foods operating income rose to $3.0 million in the first quarter from $2.1 million a year ago. Sales gained 3.5 percent to $115.5 million from $111.6 million last year.

"Overall, we're encourged by the improvements in our U.S. Foods unit," Costley said. "In Canada, we're making investments in new consumer products to grow our business. In addition, discussions are underway with potential buyers for our Canada Frozen bakery unit."
Veneuzela Foods operating earnings rose to $2.8 million in the first quarter from last year's $2.1 million, while net sales increased to $102.3 million from $71.2 million.

"While sales and earnings are up in Venezuela, our operating margins remained under pressure because of higher raw material and distribution costs," Costley said. "We expect these factors to continue to affect us in the second quarter.
